title: Contrast-aware gradient zebra for dark-mode tables
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: In dense data tables on the console, our current hard-edged zebra striping in dark themes creates harsh contrast transitions that either reduce readability for long-row reading or fail WCAG recommended contrast when brand accents are applied. This is particularly visible when brand-accented row highlights or inline chips are present.

Proposed solution: Introduce a contrast-aware gradient zebra pattern token set and a small set of component overrides for Table and DataGrid that: 1) blend alternating row backgrounds with a subtle vertical gradient and per-brand overlay to reduce perceived edge contrast; 2) adapt luminance based on the active theme and brand accent token so that WCAG AA is preserved for row text and row hover states; 3) expose a compact-variant for high-density tables that uses a shallower gradient and reduced elevation.

Technical approach:
- New tokens: table.row.zebra.gradient.start, table.row.zebra.gradient.end, table.row.zebra.overlay.alpha (per brand), table.row.hover.overlay and compact variants. Tokens are computed by the theme compiler using existing surface anchors and brand accent mixins.
- Component overrides: TableRow and TableCell will accept a theming flag (zebraMode: "gradient" | "solid" | "none") and use computed CSS variables for gradient stops and overlay alpha.
- Accessibility: Build an automated color-check step in the theme compile pipeline to run contrast checks for text and interactive elements on top of both row variants (normal and hover), failing builds if contrast < 4.5:1 for body text.
- Fallback: For environments that do not support gradients (older browsers or when prefers-reduced-motion/contrast is set), fall back to a tuned solid zebra color token that meets contrast.
acceptance_criteria: Add new theme tokens for gradient zebra start/end and per-brand overlay alpha in the token registry
TableRow/TableCell support zebraMode with JS/CSS variables and respond to theme switches without remounting
Automated contrast checks pass for all supported brand themes (default brand + 3 partner brands) in dark mode
Design review sign-off on Figma prototypes for desktop and compact density
E2E visual tests added for the top 3 table variants (default, compact, hover/highlight)
comments: 2025-02-10 Maya Chen: Initial ticket created after UX audit flagged jarring horizontal edges in dark-mode table lists. Linked Figma and initial spec. Recommended pairing with runtime token compiler changes.
2025-02-11 Priya Kapoor: Scoped to include compact variant only for first pass. Engineering dependency ENG-34121 added to include token compute helpers. Estimate 5 pts.

2025-02-12 Design review (Lars O'Neill): Feedback - reduce gradient amplitude for low-contrast brand palettes; prefer single-direction vertical gradients to avoid perceived motion; confirm hover contrast target. Action: adjust overlay alpha mapping and re-check with contrast tool.

2025-02-14 Engineering (Anika Singh): Implemented prototype in feature branch feature/table-zebra-gradient. Performance note: use CSS layering and variables to avoid repaint-heavy operations. PR opened https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4728

2025-02-16 QA (Diego Ramirez): Visual diff test created; failing case found for 'partner-blue' brand where compact variant text contrast dropped to 4.3:1 on older monitors. Suggested increase overlay alpha for compact variant when brand L* < 28.
2025-02-18 Priya Kapoor: Updated tokens in token registry per QA feedback; submitted updated Figma frames. Requesting final design review and sign-off so ENG can merge. Marking as In Review.
notes: Trade-offs: gradients slightly increase paint complexity but reduce sharp edge fatigue in dark UIs. We limit scope to vertical gradients and a small token set to keep complexity low.
Rollout plan: feature-flag behind console-2025.03; enable for internal beta and 3 partner accounts before global rollout.
Follow-ups: explore applying same overlay approach to charts (banded area) if this reduces legend/series contrast issues.
Related tickets: DES-198760 (token registry cleanup), ENG-34121 (theme token compute helpers)
